name: Occupational Therapy (OT)
addresses: Fine motor skills, sensory processing, self-care tasks (dressing, eating, handwriting), and overall participation in daily 'occupations' of childhood — play, school, self-care.

commonly_explored_for.rationale: Sensory regulation strategies and fine motor/self-care skill building.
OT is typically the primary discipline for sensory integration support.
Builds fine motor coordination and compensatory strategies for daily tasks.
Supports motor milestone development and daily living skills given global developmental delay.

typical_session_format: Usually 30-60 minutes, often play-based for younger children, in a clinic with sensory/motor equipment or at home/school. Frequency varies from weekly to a few times a week depending on need.
honest_limits: OT does not treat core social-communication differences in autism, does not diagnose conditions, and is not a substitute for medical or psychiatric care. Progress is often gradual and non-linear.

name: Speech-Language Therapy (SLT)
addresses: Spoken language (expressive and receptive), speech sound production, motor planning for speech, social communication (pragmatics), and in some cases feeding/swallowing.

commonly_explored_for.rationale: This is the primary and most intensive therapy for CAS — targets motor planning for speech directly.
Supports both functional communication and social communication/pragmatics.
Addresses absent or significantly delayed spoken language; may include augmentative communication.

typical_session_format: Usually 30-45 minutes, 1-3 times weekly depending on severity, often drill-based with high repetition for motor speech goals, or play/conversation-based for pragmatics goals.
honest_limits: SLT cannot speed up motor-planning recovery faster than a child's individual neurology allows, and consistent attendance matters more than any single technique. It does not address non-speech-related developmental concerns.

name: Behavioral Therapy
addresses: Observable behaviors — reducing behaviors that interfere with learning or safety, and building adaptive skills (communication, self-regulation, social skills) through structured, evidence-based teaching methods.

commonly_explored_for.rationale: Widely used to build communication, social, and adaptive skills; approaches vary (ABA is the most studied, though not without debate in the autism community about intensity and approach).
Behavioral strategies (routines, reinforcement systems, parent training) are a first-line, evidence-based approach, often before or alongside medication.

typical_session_format: Highly variable: from a few hours a week of parent-training-focused sessions to intensive multi-hour daily programs, depending on the specific approach and the child's needs.
honest_limits: Not every behavioral approach suits every family or child, and the autism community has real, documented debate about intensity and approach — a good provider discusses goals and approach with you, not just hours. Behavioral therapy does not change a child's underlying neurology.

name: Physical Therapy (PT)
addresses: Gross motor skills — strength, balance, coordination, gait, and overall movement function.

commonly_explored_for.rationale: Builds gross motor coordination, balance, and confidence in movement.
Supports gross motor milestone progress (sitting, walking) given hypotonia and delayed motor development.

typical_session_format: Usually 30-45 minutes, often in a gym-like clinic setting with mats, balance equipment, and age-appropriate movement games. Frequency depends on severity of motor delay.
honest_limits: PT cannot guarantee a specific motor milestone (e.g. independent walking) will be reached — progress depends heavily on the underlying condition. It addresses movement, not fine motor, speech, or sensory needs.

name: Developmental Pediatrics
addresses: The medical 'gateway' specialty for neurodevelopmental concerns — evaluation, diagnosis, coordination of the overall care team, and medical management (including medication decisions where relevant).

commonly_explored_for.rationale: Typically the specialist who provides formal diagnosis and coordinates referrals to OT/SLT/behavioral therapy.
Diagnoses ADHD and, if appropriate, discusses and manages medication options.
Coordinates genetics referrals, overall care, and connects family to the small but growing community of clinicians familiar with H3.3-related disorders.

typical_session_format: Clinic visits, typically less frequent than therapy sessions (every few months), focused on evaluation, monitoring, and care coordination rather than hands-on skill-building.
honest_limits: This is the specialty NorthStar always defers to for diagnosis and treatment decisions — it is not something this KB entry (or NorthStar generally) can substitute for.
